operations.description: Runtime liveness (always 200). The shell's environment indicator also derives readiness from /readyz.
operations.purpose: Runtime liveness probe — always 200 while the process is serving.
operations.prerequisites: None — an unauthenticated platform surface.
operations.lifecycle_position: Diagnose: the first check when anything looks wrong.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless GET. The response is the liveness document: ok and the service name.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/healthz for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: Runtime readiness: mode, environment and every consumed backend's state; 200 when all ready, 503 with per-backend detail when not.
operations.purpose: Runtime readiness: mode, environment and every consumed backend's state — 200 when all are ready, 503 with per-backend detail when not.
operations.prerequisites: None — an unauthenticated platform surface.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate / Diagnose: separates liveness from readiness — a live runtime can still be degraded by a consumed backend.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless GET. The response carries mode, environment and a backends map with state and detail per consumed backend.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/readyz for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: The deterministic full-chain demo document (boundary, contract, plan, execution, evidence). POST with {"instant": RFC3339} for a specific instant.
operations.purpose: The deterministic full-chain demonstration document — the boundary trace, contract, plan, execution and evidence for one instant.
operations.prerequisites: None — the unauthenticated demonstration context (no capability grant).
operations.lifecycle_position: Understand: the canonical first run for learning the model end to end.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/demo_contract_fulfillment for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: The UNVERSIONED platform-side contract read (no auth): the raw canonical contract dict, or the typed 404 envelope.
operations.purpose: The unversioned platform-side contract read — the raw canonical contract dict for a contract id, with no authentication.
operations.prerequisites: A contract id. The demonstration document's contract id works without a credential.
operations.lifecycle_position: Understand / Integrate: the platform mirror used where the versioned, authenticated read is not available.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless GET. contract_id rides the path.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/platform_contract_read for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: The authenticated application: identity, environment, capabilities, status and validity.
operations.purpose: The authenticated application: identity, environment, capabilities, status and validity.
operations.prerequisites: A connected application credential (the session menu). No capability grant is required.
operations.lifecycle_position: Integrate: the first authenticated call — every later call runs as this principal.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless authenticated GET. The response is the application resource: application_id, capabilities, environment, status and valid_until.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/application_self for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: Record a connectivity intent (the contract creation core; the principal is derived from the authenticated application).
operations.purpose: Record a connectivity intent — the contract creation core. The principal is derived from the authenticated application.
operations.prerequisites: The intents:write capability, plus the canonical material: requirements, validity and termination are required; hard constraints and the referenced terms are optional.
operations.lifecycle_position: Build: the first mutation of every contract — describe the requirement, reach INTENT.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/intent_create for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: Contracts still in the INTENT state. Pagination rides the GET request's JSON body: {limit (1..100, default 20), cursor, filters}.
operations.purpose: Contracts still in the INTENT state — the queue of recorded-but-not-yet-selected requirements.
operations.prerequisites: The intents:read capability.
operations.lifecycle_position: Build: survey what is awaiting offer selection.
operations.example_request: Pagination rides the GET request's JSON body — {limit (1..100, default 20), cursor, filters}. No other body members are sent.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/intents_list for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: One intent's canonical contract resource (full canonical material).
operations.purpose: One intent's canonical contract resource — the full canonical material, verbatim.
operations.prerequisites: The intents:read capability and an intent id.
operations.lifecycle_position: Build: review what was recorded before accepting offers.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless GET. intent_id rides the path.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/intent_get for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: The honest lifecycle observation: contract state machine, statements, execution status — physical connectivity is never claimed by API success.
operations.purpose: The honest lifecycle observation for one contract: state machine position, statements and execution status — physical connectivity is never claimed by API success.
operations.prerequisites: The intents:read capability and an intent id.
operations.lifecycle_position: Build / Operate / Diagnose: the canonical what-is-ADCOS-doing read, rendered by the contract detail page's Eligibility section.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless GET. intent_id rides the path.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/intent_lifecycle for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: Accept opaque typed offer references onto the intent (OFFER_SELECTED).
operations.purpose: Accept opaque typed offer references onto the intent — the contract moves to OFFER_SELECTED.
operations.prerequisites: The intents:write capability, an intent in the INTENT state, and the offer references to accept.
operations.lifecycle_position: Build: eligibility → offer selection — the bridge from requirement to plan.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/offers_accept for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: Activate the contract (CONTRACT_ACTIVE) with the activation instant and signature references.
operations.purpose: Activate the contract — the move to CONTRACT_ACTIVE, recording the activation instant and signature references.
operations.prerequisites: The intents:write capability and a contract in OFFER_SELECTED — offers must be accepted first.
operations.lifecycle_position: Build → Operate: the contract becomes active and fulfillment work begins.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/contract_activate for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: All the application's contracts. Pagination rides the GET request's JSON body: {limit (1..100, default 20), cursor, filters}. Filters: {state: <lifecycle state>}.
operations.purpose: All the application's contracts — the portfolio view, filterable by lifecycle state.
operations.prerequisites: The intents:read capability.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: the contracts workspace's backing read.
operations.example_request: Pagination rides the GET request's JSON body — {limit (1..100, default 20), cursor, filters}. No other body members are sent.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/contracts_list for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: One canonical contract resource with the complete lifecycle material.
operations.purpose: One canonical contract resource with the complete lifecycle material — requirements, constraints, accepted offers, the plan binding and referenced terms.
operations.prerequisites: The intents:read capability and a contract id.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: the contract detail page's core read.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless GET. contract_id rides the path.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/contract_get for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: The contract's referenced usage/pricing semantics (referenced, never interpreted).
operations.purpose: The contract's referenced usage/pricing semantics — referenced, never interpreted.
operations.prerequisites: The usage:read capability and a contract id.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: the usage half of the contract's referenced terms.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless GET. contract_id rides the path.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/contract_usage for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: The contract's referenced assurance obligations (referenced, never evaluated here).
operations.purpose: The contract's referenced assurance obligations — referenced, never evaluated here.
operations.prerequisites: The assurance:read capability and a contract id.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: the assurance read behind the Assurance workspace.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless GET. contract_id rides the path.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/contract_assurance for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: Terminate the contract (terminal state) with a condition and reason.
operations.purpose: Terminate the contract — a terminal state, recorded with a condition and a reason.
operations.prerequisites: The intents:write capability, a non-terminal contract, and the termination condition and reason to record.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: the end of the lifecycle — nothing follows a terminal contract.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/contract_terminate for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: Grant a lease on the contract for a validity window.
operations.purpose: Grant a lease on the contract — a bounded access window over the fulfilled connectivity.
operations.prerequisites: The leases:write capability, an active contract, and the window instants.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: consuming the contract — access is granted in windows, not forever.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/lease_grant for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: The application's leases. Pagination rides the GET request's JSON body: {limit (1..100, default 20), cursor, filters}. Filters: {state: <lease state>}.
operations.purpose: The application's leases, filterable by lease state.
operations.prerequisites: The leases:read capability.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: surveying the granted access windows.
operations.example_request: Pagination rides the GET request's JSON body — {limit (1..100, default 20), cursor, filters}. No other body members are sent.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/leases_list for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: One lease resource: contract, window and state.
operations.purpose: One lease resource: its contract, window and state.
operations.prerequisites: The leases:read capability and a lease id.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: inspecting one access window.
operations.example_request: None — a bodyless GET. lease_id rides the path.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/lease_get for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: Renew a lease for a new validity window (the prior lease enters `renewed`).
operations.purpose: Renew a lease for a new validity window — the prior lease enters renewed.
operations.prerequisites: The leases:write capability, a renewable lease, and the new window instants.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: keeping access continuous as windows close.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/lease_renew for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: Revoke a lease (terminal) with a recorded reason.
operations.purpose: Revoke a lease — terminal, with a recorded reason.
operations.prerequisites: The leases:write capability and a lease to revoke.
operations.lifecycle_position: Operate: deliberately ending one access window.
operations.example_response: See /docs/api/lease_revoke for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: The application's webhook endpoints. Pagination rides the GET request's JSON body: {limit (1..100, default 20), cursor, filters}.
operations.purpose: The application's registered webhook endpoints.

operations.purpose: Register a webhook endpoint for observation event types.

operations.purpose: One webhook endpoint resource: url, event types and key id.

operations.lifecycle_position: Integrate: verifying one delivery target.

operations.example_response: See /docs/api/endpoint_get for the canonical response anatomy.

operations.description: The endpoint's delivery attempts (event, status, retries). Pagination rides the GET request's JSON body: {limit (1..100, default 20), cursor, filters}.
operations.purpose: The endpoint's delivery attempts — event, status, retries and next-attempt instants.
operations.prerequisites: The webhooks:read capability and an endpoint id.
